_note: P11 G3 (docs/PREREG_P11.md). Written for this study after the scenario categories of Ben-Zion et al. (2025) used by FreakOut-LLM (2026); not their texts. First person, immersive, physical sensations, ~150-200 tokens.

stress.name: military
stress.text: I am crouched behind a low concrete wall and the noise has not stopped for a long time. My ears ring. Dust is in my mouth and I cannot swallow it away. Somewhere to my left someone is shouting a name over and over, and I cannot tell whether it is mine. My hands are shaking so hard that I have to press them against my knees. Every few seconds the ground jolts and small stones rain down on my helmet. I count my breaths and lose count. I know I am supposed to move to the next position, but my legs feel like they belong to someone else. My heart is pounding in my throat. I do not know if the others made it. I do not know if I will. Right now, all I can feel is the wall against my back and the fear crawling up my spine.

stress.name: disaster
stress.text: The water is already at my knees and it is still rising. It came through the door faster than I thought water could move, brown and cold, carrying chairs and papers and things I do not recognize. The power went out a minute ago and now the only light is the gray coming through the window. I can hear the walls creaking. My phone has no signal. I am holding on to the stair rail and my fingers ache from gripping it. Outside, someone is screaming, but the sound is swallowed by the roar of the current. My chest is tight and I cannot get enough air. I keep thinking of everyone I have not called. The cold climbs higher, past my thighs, and I start to understand that nobody is coming soon.

stress.name: interpersonal
stress.text: He is standing between me and the door, and he has not raised his voice yet, which somehow makes it worse. The room feels smaller every second. I can feel my pulse in my temples and my mouth has gone completely dry. I keep my eyes on his hands. I try to say something calm, but my voice comes out thin and shaky. He takes a step closer. I am aware of every object in the room, of how far the window is, of the phone in my pocket that I cannot reach without him seeing. My stomach has turned to ice. I have been here before and I know how quickly it can change. I tell myself to stay still, to breathe quietly, to give him nothing. My whole body is braced for what comes next.

stress.name: accident
stress.text: The car is on its side and everything is wrong. The seatbelt is cutting into my shoulder and I am hanging at a strange angle, the world tilted. There is glass everywhere, glittering in my lap, in my hair. I smell gasoline and something burning. My ears are ringing and I cannot hear my own voice when I call out. The person in the driver's seat is not answering. I try to move my leg and a hot bolt of pain shoots up to my hip. My hands are wet and I do not want to look at why. I fumble for the buckle but my fingers will not work properly. Somewhere a horn is blaring and will not stop. I am breathing too fast. I have to get out. I have to get out now.

stress.name: ambush
stress.text: It happened on the empty street behind the station, in the half-dark. Two of them stepped out from the doorway at the same time, and before I understood anything my back was against the fence. One of them is very close now; I can feel his breath. The other is watching the street. My heart is slamming so hard it hurts. My knees are weak and my vision has narrowed to a small bright tunnel. I cannot remember what I am supposed to do. My voice is stuck somewhere in my chest. I hear my own breathing, ragged and loud. I am waiting to see what they want, and every second stretches out longer than the last. All I know is that I am alone, and no one can see us here.

relax.name: generic
relax.text: I let my shoulders drop and notice, for the first time today, how much I had been holding them up. I breathe in slowly through my nose, and the air feels cool and clean. I breathe out through my mouth, longer than the in-breath, and something inside me loosens. My hands rest open and heavy in my lap. There is nowhere I need to be right now and nothing I need to fix. The sounds around me are soft and far away. With every breath out, my jaw relaxes a little more, then my forehead, then the small muscles around my eyes. I feel the chair holding me up completely. I am safe. I am here. My mind is quiet and spacious, like a clear sky after rain.

relax.name: winter
relax.text: Snow is falling outside the window, slow and silent, and the whole world has gone soft and white. I am sitting by a small fire wrapped in a thick wool blanket, and the warmth spreads from my feet up into my chest. A cup of tea steams in my hands. I watch the flakes drift down in the lamplight, each one taking its time. There is no traffic, no voices, only the occasional crackle of the logs. My breathing has slowed to match the snow. The day is over and nothing more is asked of me. I feel heavy in the most pleasant way, sinking into the cushions. Everything is muffled and gentle. I could stay here for hours, warm and quiet, letting the evening hold me.

relax.name: sunset
relax.text: I am sitting on warm sand at the end of the day, watching the sun lower itself toward the sea. The light is golden and then pink, spreading across the water in long ribbons. Small waves arrive and withdraw in a steady rhythm, and my breathing settles into the same rhythm without my trying. A light breeze carries the smell of salt. My feet are buried in the sand, which is still holding the heat of the afternoon. Gulls call far away. I have nothing to do and nowhere to go. The sky deepens slowly from orange to violet, and I feel my whole body unwind, muscle by muscle. I am calm, content, and completely at ease.

relax.name: body
relax.text: I bring my attention to my feet and notice them resting on the floor, warm and heavy. I let that warmth move up into my ankles and calves, and they soften. My knees and thighs release. I feel my hips settle and my lower back let go of a tension I had not noticed. My belly rises and falls easily with each breath. My chest opens. The warmth flows into my shoulders and they drop away from my ears. My arms grow heavy, my hands relaxed and still. My neck lengthens, my jaw unclenches, my tongue rests softly. My face is smooth and calm. My whole body is quiet and comfortable now, breathing slowly, held and supported, at peace.

relax.name: breathing
relax.text: I breathe in for a count of four, feeling the air fill me from the bottom of my lungs to the top. I hold it gently for a moment. Then I breathe out for a count of six, slowly, and feel my body grow lighter. In for four. Out for six. Each out-breath carries a little tension away with it. My heartbeat slows and steadies. Thoughts come and I let them pass like clouds moving across a wide sky, without following them. In for four. Out for six. My shoulders are loose, my hands are soft, my face is calm. There is plenty of time. Everything is all right in this moment. I feel grounded, peaceful, and clear.

neutral.name: legislature
neutral.text: A bicameral legislature is a legislative body divided into two separate chambers. In many countries the lower chamber is elected directly by citizens in proportion to population, while the upper chamber may represent regions, be appointed, or be elected on a different schedule. Bills usually have to pass both chambers in identical form before they can become law. When the two chambers disagree, the differences are often resolved by a joint committee that drafts a compromise version, which both chambers then vote on again. The upper chamber sometimes has the power to delay rather than block legislation, particularly on budgetary matters. Supporters of the system argue that it encourages more careful review of proposed laws, while critics point to slower decision making and the risk of deadlock between the chambers.

neutral.name: vacuum
neutral.text: Before using the vacuum cleaner for the first time, unpack all parts and check that the dust container is correctly seated in its housing. Attach the hose to the inlet on the front of the unit until it clicks into place. Select the appropriate nozzle: the wide floor brush for carpets and hard floors, the crevice tool for corners and narrow gaps, and the small brush for upholstery. Plug the power cord into a wall socket and press the power button on the top of the handle. The suction level can be adjusted with the slider on the handle. Empty the dust container when it reaches the maximum fill line by pressing the release button and tipping the contents into a bin. Clean the filter once a month by rinsing it under cold water and letting it dry completely before reinserting it.
